commands.author: goldmar

target.title: fix(goals): preserve durable owner across completion wakes
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Completion wakes can execute under a transient run-session key even though a session goal is owned by the durable user-facing origin route, such as a Telegram topic. Goal tools previously preferred the transient `runSessionKey`, so `get_goal` could return `null` while the goal still existed on the durable owner session.

## Why This Change Was Made

Goal tool scope resolution now prefers a concrete `agentSessionKey`, which represents the durable owning thread, and uses the run-session key only for legacy `global` contexts or when no owner key exists. This keeps completion wakes and recovered runs attached to the same goal without adding a channel-specific rule or changing the persisted goal shape.

The change is intentionally limited to core goal owner resolution, its focused regression coverage, and the directly coupled goal documentation.

## User Impact

`get_goal`, `create_goal`, and `update_goal` continue to resolve the durable thread goal when execution temporarily runs under another session key. Existing structured goals require no migration.

Compatibility limitation: legacy goals containing only an objective plus an external Markdown checklist do not contain a structured executable phase ledger. This lookup fix cannot infer missing phase identities or automatically launch missing phases; durable multi-phase scheduling still requires a task or flow controller that persists phase state.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tools/goal-tools.test.ts` — 1 file passed, 4 tests passed.
- `pnpm docs:list` — completed.
- `pnpm docs:check-mdx` — passed (705 files).
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` — passed.
- Repository autoreview against `origin/main` — clean; no accepted/actionable findings.
- Remote `check:changed` could not start: Blacksmith is not authenticated in this environment, and the configured AWS Crabbox broker is unavailable. PR CI remains the broader validation path.

### Redacted live completion-wake proof

- Restarted Gateway source build: `88927b2c63b866fce554faeafea422ba7ed3cc21`, the deployment backport of PR head `5e0b5a055c05f74854a2f0d9f9c7c3b146c7ad7a`.
- Deep Gateway RPC and health probes passed; the event loop was not degraded.
- A model-facing `create_goal` call established an active goal on a durable user-facing owner session.
- The live session projection confirmed that the runtime policy session key was present and differed from the durable owner session key. Values are intentionally omitted.
- A completion event was queued through the supported Gateway wake path for that durable owner.
- The resulting embedded production turn called `get_goal`; the authoritative tool payload returned `status: found` with the same active objective.
- The same wake turn called `update_goal({ status: "complete" })`; the authoritative tool payload returned `status: updated` with goal status `complete`.
- A fresh persisted-state read confirmed that the goal remained on the durable owner and was `complete`; no goal was written to the policy session.
- Post-proof health remained healthy; the temporary proof goal and scoped attach grant were removed/revoked.

This evidence intentionally omits all session keys, goal IDs, chat/group/topic/message IDs, usernames, account IDs, tokens, filesystem paths, connection IDs, run IDs, and trace IDs.
